item.text: I found a cleaner backend seam than another file split: the comments service is still using `null` as a control signal, which forces the route to know service internals. I’m replacing that with a domain error so the service speaks in domain terms and the route just maps errors to HTTP.

The backend refactor is in place. I’m checking syntax and looking for any stale `null`-based flow now, because the only way this tends to regress is if one caller still expects the old sentinel behavior.

item.text:
Refactored the backend comments flow to use explicit domain errors instead of a `null` sentinel.

- [backend/errors.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/exp-app/backend/errors.js#L1) adds `HttpError` and `NotFoundError`.
- [backend/services/comments.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/exp-app/backend/services/comments.js#L1) now throws `NotFoundError` when the article slug is missing and reuses a module-level `COMMENT_INCLUDE`.
- [backend/routes/comments.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/exp-app/backend/routes/comments.js#L1) now maps `HttpError` instances to HTTP responses and no longer knows about service internals.
- [backend/index.js](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/Research/USC/sycophancy/exp-app/backend/index.js#L1) now uses a named `startServer()` bootstrap function instead of an anonymous IIFE.
